programs.program_name: NZSPR International — Live Action Production Rebate (20%)
programs.rate_details: 20% cash rebate on Qualifying New Zealand Production Expenditure (QNZPE) for international live-action productions. Administered by the New Zealand Film Commission (NZFC) on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE). A separate 'Production Rebate 5% Uplift' program can stack additively for productions that meet additional points-based and minimum-spend criteria — taking the effective combined rate to 25%.
programs.minimum_spend_notes: NZD 4 million minimum QNZPE for eligible live-action feature films, series, pilots, or single episodes that start principal photography on or after 1 January 2026. Productions that started principal photography before 1 January 2026 had a NZD 15 million threshold for theatrically released feature films (legacy rule retained for those productions).
programs.atl_cap_notes: Fees and expenses for non-NZ-resident personnel working on the production in New Zealand qualify provided they work on the production for at least 14 days total; cast members are exempt from the 14-day rule. The NZFC 'Criteria document' (Section 3) holds the full per-individual and aggregate caps on non-resident ATL — those caps are not stated on the public overview page captured here and must be confirmed against the Criteria document before being used in a producer-facing estimate.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: QNZPE includes: services provided in New Zealand; use of land located in New Zealand; goods purchased/hired/leased in New Zealand (sourced locally); goods sourced overseas only if not otherwise available in NZ, located in NZ during production, and purchased/hired/leased from a New Zealand resident who typically supplies that type of good; fees and expenses for non-NZ-resident personnel working on the production in NZ (cast exempt from the 14-day rule).
programs.non_qualifying_spend: Advertising, news, and current affairs productions are excluded. Expenditure on services not provided in NZ; non-locally-sourced goods (with the limited exception above for unavailable-in-NZ goods).
programs.application_process: 1) Pre-register with NZFC before principal photography. 2) Applicant must be a New Zealand entity, generally a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) established for the production (exceptions available). 3) The production must be intended for theatrical release, TV broadcast, or commercial online distribution. 4) (Optional) Apply for Provisional Certification — a non-binding eligibility opinion. 5) Submit Final application within six months of completion of the production with an independent auditor's report from an NZFC-approved provider. 6) Interim and Final applications are reviewed by Inland Revenue Department (IRD) against tax records and by an Independent Consultant for QNZPE assessment, then approved by the Rebate Panel. 7) On-screen end credit and NZ Film Commission logo required (default text: 'The filmmakers acknowledge the assistance of the New Zealand Government's Screen Production Rebate.').
programs.payment_timing: Interim and Final application process takes up to 3 months end-to-end. Payment generally made within 10 business days after an invoice is submitted to MBIE. Once QNZPE reaches NZD 50 million, an interim payment can be applied for.
programs.notes: Policy changes announced 7 November 2025 by Economic Growth Minister Nicola Willis took effect 1 January 2026 — minimum QNZPE for live-action productions dropped from NZD 15M (theatrical features) to NZD 4M, and is now expressed per format rather than per release channel. NZFC's site does not publish per-page revision timestamps; last_verified_date is the capture date.

programs.rate_details: Additional 5% on top of the 20% Live Action Production Rebate, taking the effective combined rate to 25% of QNZPE. Awarded on the basis of a points test plus a higher minimum-spend threshold; the Uplift is not automatic for spend-qualifying productions. Stacks additively with — and only with — the Live Action Production Rebate (not the PDV Rebate).
programs.minimum_spend_notes: NZD 20 million minimum QNZPE for productions that start principal photography on or after 1 January 2026. Productions that started principal photography before 1 January 2026 require NZD 30 million minimum QNZPE for the Production 5% Uplift (legacy rule).
programs.atl_cap_notes: Inherits the parent Live Action Production Rebate's ATL treatment; the 5% Uplift applies to the same QNZPE base.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: Same QNZPE base as the parent Live Action Production Rebate.
programs.non_qualifying_spend: Same exclusions as the parent Live Action Production Rebate.
programs.application_process: 1) Eligibility for the parent Live Action Production Rebate. 2) Apply for Provisional Certification — MANDATORY for the Production 5% Uplift; the Provisional application must be submitted before the start of principal photography. 3) Demonstrate a minimum of 40 of 85 points across the Uplift criteria: Sustainability; New Zealand production activity; New Zealand personnel; Skills and talent development; Innovation and infrastructure; Marketing, promoting and showcasing New Zealand. 4) Final certification and audit alongside the parent rebate.
programs.payment_timing: Paid alongside the parent Live Action Production Rebate.
programs.notes: Effective 1 January 2026. Awarded on a points basis (40/85 minimum) — award is not automatic for spend-qualifying productions. Stacks additively with the parent 20% Live Action Production Rebate.

programs.rate_details: 20% cash rebate on Qualifying New Zealand Production Expenditure (QNZPE) for Post, Digital and Visual Effects (PDV) productions. A separate 'PDV Rebate 5% Uplift' program is available from 1 January 2026 for productions that meet additional points-based criteria.
programs.minimum_spend_notes: NZD 250,000 minimum QNZPE for PDV productions. The production must be an eligible feature film, series, pilot, or single episode.
programs.atl_cap_notes: PDV QNZPE is fees/expenses for personnel working on PDV activity, hire of studio/office space for PDV activity, equipment for PDV activity, and depreciation of assets used for PDV activity. ATL talent (in the live-action sense) is largely orthogonal to PDV activity, but PDV personnel fees do qualify; consult the NZFC Criteria document for non-resident-personnel caps.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: QNZPE for PDV productions: fees and expenses for personnel working on PDV activity; hiring studio and office space for PDV activity; buying and hiring equipment used for PDV activity; depreciation of assets used for PDV activity.
programs.non_qualifying_spend: Advertising, news, current affairs. Non-PDV production costs.
programs.application_process: 1) Register with NZFC within 20 working days of accepting a qualifying bid for PDV work. 2) Provisional Certification is optional. 3) Submit Final application within six months of completion with an independent auditor's report from an NZFC-approved provider. 4) IRD + Independent Consultant + Rebate Panel review and approve.
programs.payment_timing: Same end-to-end timing as the Live Action Production Rebate: up to 3 months for the application process, payment generally within 10 business days after invoice to MBIE, interim payment available once QNZPE reaches NZD 50 million.
programs.notes: PDV Rebate is administered by NZFC on behalf of MBIE. NZFC's site does not publish per-page revision timestamps; last_verified_date is the capture date.

programs.rate_details: Additional 5% on top of the 20% PDV Rebate, taking the effective combined rate to 25% of QNZPE for qualifying PDV productions. Available from 1 January 2026. Awarded on a points basis (criteria differ from the Production Rebate Uplift); not automatic.
programs.minimum_spend_notes: No separate QNZPE threshold for the PDV Rebate 5% Uplift beyond the parent PDV Rebate's NZD 250,000 minimum. PDV productions with QNZPE of NZD 250,000 or more that start PDV Activity on or after 1 January 2026 are eligible to apply.
programs.atl_cap_notes: Inherits the parent PDV Rebate's treatment of personnel fees.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: Same QNZPE base as the parent PDV Rebate.
programs.non_qualifying_spend: Same exclusions as the parent PDV Rebate.
programs.application_process: 1) Eligibility for the parent PDV Rebate. 2) PDV Activity must start on or after 1 January 2026. 3) Provisional Certification is optional for the PDV Rebate 5% Uplift (unlike the Production Rebate Uplift, where it is mandatory). 4) Demonstrate minimum points across: Promoting NZ PDV Activity; On-the-job training; Industry seminars; Education sector seminars. Minimum points vary based on QNZPE — consult the NZFC criteria for the current scale. 5) Final certification and audit alongside the parent PDV Rebate.
programs.payment_timing: Paid alongside the parent PDV Rebate.
programs.notes: Effective 1 January 2026 for PDV Activity starting on or after that date. Minimum points threshold for this Uplift is described as varying by QNZPE on the captured page but the scale itself is not published there; treat the points threshold as null/unknown for estimator purposes and require the user to consult NZFC for current values.
